The band percentages sum to about 100% (81.30+14.95+2.80+0.93), so the severe band was taken as 0. 3) The Discussion (p.4) says '0.93% had extremely severe misophonia, 9.34% had moderate misophonia, and 5.60% had mild misophonia'. This contradicts the Results and Table 1 (mild 14.95%, N=16; moderate 2.80%, N=3); Table 1 and the Results were used. 4) Text and Table 1 call the top band 'highly severe' and also 'extremely severe'. 5) Sex band counts back-calculate exactly (female 61/10/2/1 of 74; male 26/6/1/0 of 33) and sum to the overall 87/16/3/1. 6) Urban/rural bands are inconsistent: urban 82.43+16.41+1.35 = 100.19%, and 16.41% x 74 is not an integer. Rural (27/3/2/1 of 33) plus urban (61/12/1/0 of 74) gives subclinical 88 and mild 15, against 87 and 16 overall. Rural/urban subgroups were not extracted because they are not sex, age or clinical subgroups (rural 33/140 and urban 74/201, both on the L0 'misophonia' definition). 7) The '31.37% misophonia' (107/341) counts subclinical scorers as cases, and the case threshold is never stated.
